notes.title: Solasta Spring Update & Dungeon Maker - Patch Notes
notes.content:
[i]Hey there folks![/i]

[i]The Spring Update should now be live, with a plethora of changes and new content! With the addition of the difficulty options, side quests and background quests, your Solastan experience is getting closer and closer to the final release. Well bugs and polish aside of course, Early Access has proved quite effective at finding and squashing them so far! But enough talk, it's time to dive into the patch notes.[/i]

[previewyoutube=2ZJ89PET_Qg;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2][b]Old Save Files are NOT compatible [/b][/h2]
As stated in our previous articles, due to changes in existing systems [b]save files from previous versions will NOT be compatible with the Spring Update[/b]. That said, we're adding a lot of side content in this new update, so restarting a fresh run will give a new experience where you don't have to run after the main quest! 

Note that [b]we will put the previous version of the game (January Update) on a separate Steam branch[/b] so that you can keep playing with your old saves if you want to. And although one is never safe from a bad surprise during Early Access, save compatibility should hopefully be preserved from the Spring Update onwards.

[h2][b]Spring Patch Sales & Price Increase[/b][/h2]
[b]Solasta will be discounted when the Spring Update hits the store on March 25th until March 31st, after which the price of the game will increase from $35 to $40 in anticipation of the 1.0 release.[/b] This is due to the fact that Steam prevents games from discounting within 30 days of a price increase, so we unfortunately cannot increase the price when 1.0 gets released while also having a launch discount. So if you want to jump in Solasta at Early Access price, make sure you don't miss the Spring Update sales! 

[h1][b]New Content / Feature:[/b][/h1]
[list]	[*][b]Added the Dungeon Maker (Beta). [/b]The Dungeon Maker allows you to create, share and play custom maps, and will continue to get improved over time. Check the Dungeon Maker section below for more information. [/*]	[*][b]The Main Quest now continues a little bit past the Wizard's Tower. [/b]You will be able to return to Caer Cyflen to report to the Council and will unlock your own residence (simply a resting area, not customizable), after which you will be free to continue playing instead of being booted back to the main menu. [/*]	[*][b]Added Background Quests[/b] for each of the 8 Backgrounds available in Character Creation. Background Quests are only available if one of the party member has the right Background - for instance, the Spy Background unlocks the Spy Background Quest. You can check [url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/120-spring-update-planned-for-march-25th]where to unlock them in the following article[/url].[/*]	[*][b]Added Side Quests[/b]. Side Quests are available through the Adventuring Board found in Caer Cyflen close to Gorim's Emporium, with the first unlocking once you talked to the Council after returning from Caer Lem. Be warned, some Side Quests may be quite difficult if you tackle them immediately after unlocking them! [/*]	[*][b]Added Difficulty Settings[/b]. Difficulty Settings can be found the in the Settings => Game tab and can be customized at any time. Note that higher difficulty modes have not yet been properly balanced yet, so playing on Cataclysm may very well make you want to eat your keyboard (please don't).[/*]	[*][b]Implemented Legendary Actions for Aksha and Razan.[/b] Legendary Actions allow certain bosses to act outside their turn, so you may have to change your tactics a bit![/*]	[*][b]Added Achievements (WIP)[/b]. Note that some achievements may not be unlockable until the full 1.0 release - such as the achievement for finishing the game. [/*]	[*][b]Added new Martial Feats [/b]and rebalanced a couple of existing ones. [url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/119-spring-update-coming-soon-whats-in-it]Read more about them here[/url].[/*][/list]
[h2][b]The Dungeon Maker (Beta)[/b][/h2]
[previewyoutube=WkArBjQNIDM;full][/previewyoutube]
The Dungeon Maker is an in-game tool available directly in the main menu which allows you to create, edit and play custom maps. The video above is a quickstart guide - if you need a more in-depth guide, [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/forum/dungeon-maker-user-manual]it is available in our Forums over there[/url]. 

[h3][b]How do I share the dungeons I created? [/b][/h3]
You can access your custom dungeon folder by simply clicking the [url=https://www.solasta-game.com/storage/cms/9S1XobaYAqAEtonUnvFnKGuiaPNqSYOYkdi8Ib59.png]in-game "[b]Browse Files[/b]" button[/url] in the Dungeon Maker menu. The folder can also be manually found there: [code]C:/User/_YourUserName_/AppData/LocalLow/Tactical Adventures/Solasta/UserContent/Locations[/code]
Whenever you create a map in the Dungeon Maker, the game will create a .json file containing all the information with the same name there.

[h3][b]Where do I share the dungeons I created?[/b][/h3]
For the moment we're still working on Steam Workshop Integration. In the meantime, you could always drop by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/solastacrownofthemagister/]good ol' NexusMod where many other mods are already available[/url] (reminder: mods are community driven, Tactical Adventures has no control over them and cannot guarantee that they work properly). 

[h3][b]How do I play a dungeon I just downloaded?[/b][/h3]
Simply copy paste the .json file into you custom dungeon folder, that you can either access by clicking the [url=https://www.solasta-game.com/storage/cms/9S1XobaYAqAEtonUnvFnKGuiaPNqSYOYkdi8Ib59.png]in-game "[b]Browse Files[/b]" button[/url] in the Dungeon Maker menu, or manually opening [code]C:/User/_YourUserName_/AppData/LocalLow/Tactical Adventures/Solasta/UserContent/Locations[/code]
The new dungeon should then appear in-game in the Dungeon Maker list. 

[h3][b]I have a question about the Dungeon Maker![/b][/h3]
Make sure you read the [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/forum/dungeon-maker-user-manual]in-depth forum guide about the Dungeon Maker[/url], and if you still have questions feel free to [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]swing by our Discord server and head to the #modding channel[/url]!

[h3][b]Will you update for the Dungeon Maker in the future?[/b][/h3]
Of course! You might have noticed the Dungeon Maker is still lacking quite a few features, and that's because the Dungeon Maker will still be in beta when we release the full 1.0 version of Solasta (we've got to make sure we wrap up the main campaign properly first). There are tons of things we want to add later - quest systems, dialogs, merchants, more environments... Make sure you tell us what you'd like to see first!

tags.feature: Added the Dungeon Maker (Beta).
The Main Quest now continues a little bit past the Wizard's Tower.
Added Background Quests for each of the 8 Backgrounds available in Character Creation.
Added Side Quests.
Added Difficulty Settings.
Implemented Legendary Actions for Aksha and Razan.
Added Achievements (WIP).
Added new Martial Feats and rebalanced a couple of existing ones.

tags.balance_change: Increased max level cap from level 6 to level 8.
Adjusted Sorak Skirmishers, Sorak Warriors and Sorak Saboteurs stats to further differentiate them.

tags.bug: IMPORTANT: A mistake snuck in at the last moment and Sorak Saboteurs have incorrectly been granted the power to Sneak Attack (2d6), which can make them extremely dangerous in combination with their Doom Laughter Power.

tags.feature: The Major Teleportation Gates are now fully functional!

The following spells have been added: Animal Friendship (Green Mage), Entangle (Green Mage), Giant Insect (Green Mage), Freedom of Movement, Wind Wall, Banishment, Black Tentacles, Blight, Conjure Minor Elementals, Death Ward, Dimension Door, Fire Shield, Greater Invisibility, Ice Storm, Identify Creatures, Phantasmal Killer, Stoneskin, Wall of Fire.

The following feats have been added: Ambidextrous, Discretion of Coedymwarth, Eager for Battle, Follow Up Strike, Hauler (reworked), Might of the Iron Legion (reworked), Powerful Cantrip (reworked), Raise Shield, Rush to Battle, Sturdiness of the Tundra, Take Aim, Twin Blade, Uncanny Accuracy (reworked)

tags.balance_change: Removed one enemy from the first Sorak encounter in Caer Lem Caves.
Removed one enemy from the Crown Room encounter in Tower of Magic.

tags.bug: Fixed Fly not allowing players to reach treasure chests in some areas.
Character Proficiency screen should now correctly display bonuses to ability checks
Oil of Sharpness can no longer be applied during combat, as it takes one minute to do so.
Attempting to cast a concentration spell from a scroll while already concentrating on a spell will now correctly display a warning message.
Items are no longer automatically equipped when transferred between characters.

tags.balance_change: Monsters will now respect the spellcasting rules just like adventurers, they've been barred from casting two spells and are now correctly restricted to spell + cantrip when using their bonus action.

tags.bug: Large monsters such as Giant Spiders should no longer be able to attack much higher than their model would suggest.
Save Files should now be smaller in size
Spellcasters should now be able to use scrolls directly from their inventory during combat

tags.balance_change: Feared characters will now run a bit less far so you don't have to spend multiple turns chasing after their fleeing butt
Adjusted Minotaur AI so it's a little more agressive, its axe has your name on it.
Refined AI spell usage to avoid spellcasters automatically unleashing all their most powerful spells at the start of the fight

tags.bug: Game Over screen when caught during stealth tutorial will now correctly tell you that you got spotted instead of telling you that you died (although let's be honest, you very likely died as a result of getting spotted anyway).

tags.feature: Added Steamworks and GOG Galaxy Integration - note that Steam Workshop hasn't been implemented yet, we'll try to get that done for the full 1.0 release.

tags.balance_change: Arrows & Bolts which hit their their target now have a 50% chance to be recoverable after the fight on their body

tags.feature: Belt of Dwarvenkind now has a chance to add a beard to characters who attune to it

tags.bug: Ranged weapon attacks which miss now properly... well... miss the target. Instead of the target going all Matrix style and dodging the arrow.

tags.feature: Added some new crafting recipe and spell scrolls
Bestiary now includes monsters' passive abilities (like Child of Darkness)

tags.balance_change: Made many adjustments to loot tables, chests and merchants

tags.feature: Added many different poisons
Added smithing tools to craft bolts and arrows

tags.balance_change: Beefed up Razan to make him stronger than Aksha
Defiler's "Darkness" have been replaced by "Dark Veil"

tags.bug: Fixed Defilers draining maximum HP on non-necrotic damage inflicted.

It is no longer possible to ready a cantrip if you shouldn't be able to cast it due to component restrictions (Vocal, Somatic, Material)

Greenmage Magic Arrow Feature no longer trigger on Firebolt

notes.title: Spring Update planned for March 25th!
notes.content:
[i]Hey there folks,[/i]

[i]We know you're eager to have a go at Solasta's Spring Update, so we're just going to come clean with the date. You'll be able to enjoy everything we've been talking about the last few weeks on Thursday March 25th - including the brand new Dungeon Maker. Alright, now for more information about this upcoming patch...[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/57e01d7cfee6e2f15f0731d4bd944194a24c0886.jpg[/img]
[i]Home office perk: Warming your lap with cats. Provides heating and relaxation![/i]

[h2][b]Spring Update Community Stream[/b][/h2]
As per usual, [b]we'll be hosting a stream on Twitch to accompany the update[/b]. Join us on the day before the patch, [b]Wednesday March 24th, at 9 am PDT / 12 pm EDT / 5 pm CET[/b] to discover the new content at our side and ask us any question you can think of! The participants this time will be Mathieu, Creative Director, Xavier, Gameplay Director, Pierre, Marketing Director and myself Emile, Community Lead. [b]Make sure to [url=https://www.twitch.tv/tacticaladventures]follow us on Twitch[/url] so that you don't miss the stream![/b]

[url=https://www.twitch.tv/tacticaladventures][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/8342a9fd76721feb31dfc8fb2485594accfed849.png[/img][/url]	
[i]We'll mostly be playing around with the Dungeon Maker and show a few sidequests, then we'll be taking requests![/i]

[h2][b]Reminder: Save Files Compatibility![/b][/h2]
As stated in the previous update, we want to remind everyone that [b]save files will become [/b][b]incompatible [/b]with the Spring Update, so you'll have to start fresh! For those who want to finish their current run, [b]we will put the previous version of the game (January Update) on a separate Steam branch[/b] so that you can keep playing if you want to.

[h2][b]Background Quests[/b][/h2]
In this Spring Update, we'll be solidifying and enlarging the foundations of the house rather than building a new floor. For those who aren't used to having bards or pompous wizards in their party, that meant [b]we won't be adding new quests to the main campaign in this update[/b], to avoid spoiling too much of the story before the release of the full game. 

... Well, truth be told we are adding a bit more to the main campaign: [b]you'll now be able to come back from the Wizard's Tower[/b] and talk to the Council at Caer Cyflen, after which if you try to continue the main storyline you'll meet the End of Early Access message. But this time, it won't send you to the main menu - [b]you'll be free to explore the world and take on side quests[/b]! Indeed, you will no longer be limited to the main story quests, with the addition of[b] 8 backgrounds quests [/b]which will give you a little more insight about the past of your party members, depending on the backgrounds you picked during Character Creation. [b]Those quests are fully fleshed out with dialogs and new locations[/b], and will be available at different times.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/57f93d41b09e80ed8432a7e34883bd0abda5bc29.png[/img]
[i]The Aristocrat Quest will drag you into a little conflict about inheritance, but not everyone will play fair...[/i]
[list]	[*][b]Acolyte[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from the [b]Wizard's Tower[/b], provided the party picked up [b]Emtan's Journal[/b] when visiting the ruined Monastery[/*]	[*][b]Aristocrat[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from the [b]Wizard's Tower[/b][/*]	[*][b]Academic[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from [b]Tower of Magic[/b][/*]	[*][b]Lawkeeper[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from the [b]Wizard's Tower[/b][/*]	[*][b]Lowlife[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from [b]Caer Lem[/b][/*]	[*][b]Philosopher[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from the [b]Wizard's Tower[/b][/*]	[*][b]Sellsword[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from the [b]Wizard's Tower[/b][/*]	[*][b]Spy[/b]: Unlocks after talking to the council once back from the [b]Wizard's Tower[/b][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/3d794473431fdb7b35071ddae392e4982237cdcf.png[/img]
[i]The Lowlife Quest will make use of your former connections to find something that was stolen, though you might run into a bit of trouble too...[/i]

[b]Note that the background quests are not equal in difficulty[/b] (some unlock much earlier than others) - [b]and may be challenging if tackled immediately when unlocked![/b] We still need to polish the difficulty there, so [b]we're looking forward to your feedback on these newly added background quests[/b]. Also, for those who may not remember the Wizard's Tower is the location that previously marked the end of the Early Access.

[h2][b]Adventuring Board[/b][/h2]
The Background Quests isn't the only thing that will make you squeeze more hours out of Solasta (well, aside from the Dungeon Maker and the custom dungeons people will be making). [b]We now have an Adventuring Board where you can take a break from saving the world and get to help the local populace![/b] These small quests will encourage you to go back to previously visited locations and will feature new encounters. Now don't worry - while these quests will help you get some more experience and items, you can absolutely focus on the main campaign and forget about them if that's not your thing. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/1aff294a8ad51ed102973888cd8a07591c91b32e.png[/img]
[i]I get to slay more monsters AND I get paid for it? I love this job.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/a2776861df979cf07d67749b910f7cb2ce3eb0ea.png[/img]
[i]Caer Lem after the outpost has been re-established and (tentatively) repared[/i]

[h2][b]Let's Talk Difficulty[/b][/h2]
Are you scared that all of these changes we previously talked about will be making the game too easy? My oh my, don't be. First of all, remember that [b]we're adding [/b][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/117-cracking-open-the-difficulty-settings][b]difficulty settings[/b][/url][b] in this update[/b]  - meaning that if you find the game too simple, don't hesitate to crank up a few notches. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/cf437476351b4a4f3e767d87da873e9c1094da21.png[/img]
[i]You can find Difficulty Settings in the "Game" Tab when changing the settings[/i]

Second, keep in mind [b]we still need to do a final balance pass before the full release of the game[/b] - so some encounters that you consider too easy or too hard may very well be different when 1.0 hits the store, nothing is set in stone. While some fights may be easy on purpose (for story reasons or simply because we know the next long rest is still quite far away), some simply haven't been revisited yet by the design team.  

Third... [b]Some bosses will now have access to legendary actions[/b]. For those who may not be familiar with the tabletop ruleset, some powerful creatures have access to legendary actions which allow them to act outside of their turn - usually right after a party member acts.[b] In the Early Access, the two bosses with legendary actions are Aksha and Razvan[/b] - you will need to tackle these fights with care or you'll regret it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/9d72942a795c833d8f838c592be738537d5d6981.png[/img]	
[i]Aksha using a Legendary Action to cast Dark Veil outside her own turn[/i]

[b]Remember that you can change the [/b][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/117-cracking-open-the-difficulty-settings][b]different difficulty sliders[/b][/url][b] (not just the preset) at any time, even during combat[/b]. If an encounter is particularly tough, don't hesitate to tune down a few difficulty options and revert them to normal after the fight is over. [b]Note: Currently all the settings, including difficulty ones as you can change them at any time, are saved game-wide.[/b] This means if you set your game difficulty to "Scavenger" and load a save, you will still be in "Scavenger" difficulty regardless of what the difficulty setting was when you made that save. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/6816caad29936c9b9c09547ea30b111b54b41ee5.png[/img]
[i]You can change a whole lot of things, including attack modifiers if you feel like it's too hard to hit your foes[/i]

[h2][b]Preserve Random Seed - Changing the Timeline[/b][/h2]
In this update, [b]we have decided to turn "Preserve Random Seed" off by default[/b] when launching Solasta for the first time (it used to be on by default). Too many players were unaware of this being an option and were struggling in some encounters where they had a really rough start, making them think the RNG gods were dancing on their grave by forcing them to roll poorly. 

[b]For some who may not understand what "Preserve Random Seed" did, think of it like time travel[/b]. When activated, you stay in the same timeline: If you look through the window and see a bird landing on a branch, then go back in time and look through the window again, you'll see the same bird landing on that same branch at the same moment. However when deactivated, you go into a different timeline every time you load - whenever you'll look through the window, the bird may not land on the same branch, it may be a different bird, or there might be no bird whatsoever. [b]To go back to Solasta: with "Preserve Random Seed" on, if you roll 5 on your attack roll and reload, you'll roll 5 again on that same attack every time (the timeline remains the same). With "Preserve Random Seed" off, you may roll a 12 after reloading, or 18, or 2, or even 5 again.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/03a18daedea8beee781e3104891ffe133670ffd6.png[/img]
[i]This is where you can find Preserve Random Seed in the option menu[/i]

This means before the patch, some unlucky players ended up with terrible rolls on their first round and had one character die straight away, making them reload and... see the same things happening again. Now with the option off by default, this will no longer be the case. [b]You might wonder, why was it on by default in the first place? Well, almost all tacticals - such as XCOM, or Final Fantasy Tactics - preserve random seed[/b]. There are multiple of reasons why. For instance, it encourages players to not reload every time they have a bad roll (since the player knows they can't get out of it), saving time in the long run and making them play with the consequences of their action. It also encourages the player to change their approach instead of brute forcing the save/reload option for better rolls - if a frontal confrontation doesn't work out, maybe it's time to use the dodge action on that frontline fighter and not just keep pressing that attack button, or cast Shield of Faith for more AC instead of Guiding Bolt for more damage. 

[b]That being said, we also understand that most RPGs don't have the issues it brings up - and Solasta is a Tactical RPG, not just a tactical[/b], which is why we've decided to turn that option off by default. [b]We invite everyone to give your feedback on that decision, as our hearts still waver between the two options for the full release[/b] - both having strong arguments for and against. [b]Note that "Preserve Random Seed" will always be available in the game settings, we're just talking about the default setting of that option. [/b]

[h2][b]Bug Fixes for Everyone![/b][/h2]
[b]As usual when we release a large patch, it will be full of bug fixes! [/b]Things like Rangers and Paladins not being able to use scrolls, fear and paralysis not allowing you to roll a saving throw at the end of each turn or the game sending the cleric instead of the rogue to disarm traps should now hopefully be a thing of the past. Clear the way old bugs, and make way for new bugs that the Spring Update will bring - hopefully smaller and less annoying ones though. 

[h2][b]Achievements Incoming (WIP)[/b][/h2]
Some of you may have noticed a lone hidden achievement popping up a few weeks ago on Solasta. That was us testing around to make sure the system was working properly (unfortunately, Steam achievements can only be tested live). Now, you can probably imagine what's coming next!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/930419a90317d22079c43a16ad3605c9a4bb5d95.png[/img]
[i]We're still missing the icons for now, but don't worry everything will be ready by the time we release the full game![/i]

Achievements, that's what! Yes that was quite obvious, I know. [b]The entire list of achievements will be coming to Steam and GOG in the Spring Update[/b], although they are still being worked on - [b]the icons and localization are still missing for now, though they are still 100% functional[/b] (meaning you can unlock them normally). Note that not all achievements can be... well... achieved, due to the fact that some require you to complete quests that are not available in the Early Access version of Solasta, so you'll have to wait until the full launch to get these ones. Regardless, have fun hunting them down!

[h2][b]Spring Update Discount & Price Increase[/b][/h2]
[b]Solasta will be discounted[/b][b] when the Spring Update hits the store on March 25th until March 31st, after which the price of the game will increase from $35 to $40 in anticipation of the 1.0 release.[/b] This is due to the fact that Steam prevents games from discounting within 30 days of a price increase, so we unfortunately cannot increase the price when 1.0 gets released while also having a launch discount. So if you want to jump in Solasta at Early Access price, make sure you don't miss the Spring Update sales!

[b]Alright folks, this is the end for today! See you on March 25th - or 24th if you're joining our Dev Stream. [/b][b]Thank you for reading, and don't hesitate to drop by [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/]our Forums[/url] or [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]our Discord Server[/url].[/b]

[b]Read our previous articles here:[/b]
[list]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/119-spring-update-coming-soon-whats-in-it]Spring Update, coming soon! What's in it?[/url][/*]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/118-dungeon-maker-showcase-create-your-own-dungeons]Dungeon Maker Showcase - Create your own Dungeons![/url][/*]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/117-cracking-open-the-difficulty-settings]Cracking Open The Difficulty Settings[/url][/*][/list]

notes.title: Spring Update, coming soon! What's in it?
notes.content:
[i]Hey hey hey,[/i]

[i]Now that the Dungeon Maker has been revealed, it's time for more good news. We will be releasing a Spring Update soon - in a matter of weeks! Exciting news isn't it, now stay with me for a bit longer to read about the upcoming content that you'll be able to enjoy... At least some of it! You'll have to come back next week for a date and the rest of the exciting changes we'll be bringing to Solasta now that Winter is over![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/e325a65f330adaa930a88a3cdffb4429e86a4566.png[/img]
[i]As you can see here, the entire Tactical Adventures team is hard at work to bring you the Spring Update[/i]

[h2][b]Important Note: Save Files Compatibility![/b][/h2]
Unfortunately as you may well remember, we've always said that there might be a point during Early Access where [b]save files become [/b][b]incompatible [/b]with a new update... And [b]this will be the case for the Spring [/b][b]Update[/b]. As we revamped many systems in the background, we had to break things to move forward.

Now the good thing is, [b]this should be the only time it happens before the 1.0 [/b][b]launch - and on top of that, load times are now significantly faster[/b]. Also, we're adding a lot of side content in this new update, so restarting a fresh run will give a new experience where you don't have to run after the main quest! 

For those who want to finish their current run, [b]we will put the previous version of the game (January Update) on a separate Steam branch[/b] so that you can keep playing if you want to.

[h2][b]Dungeon Maker, coming through![/b][/h2]
Many of you have been asking when you would be able to try out the Dungeon Maker - well, wonder no more! [b]The Dungeon Maker will be included in the Spring Update[/b], and will be directly accessible from the in-game main menu. [b]Keep in mind that we're working on the Dungeon Maker[/b] and that it will still be in beta when Solasta 1.0 launches, as we're still prioritizing the main campaign above all!

[previewyoutube=WkArBjQNIDM;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/c7ed0b532e76ba182b99428e83699d5655989f8a.jpg[/img]
[i]Here's a screenshot of the updated Dungeon Maker UI, which will be available in the upcoming update[/i]

As a reminder, [b]you can read more about the Dungeon Maker in [/b][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/118-dungeon-maker-showcase-create-your-own-dungeons][b]our previous [/b][b]article[/b][/url], which goes over several questions regarding the tool. [url=https://wccftech.com/solasta-crown-of-the-magister-qa-making-dungeons-with-dd-5ths-ruleset/][b]Our interview with Wccftech[/b][/url][b] is also a good source of information [/b]as it is fairly lengthy and detailed! 

[h2][b]New Martial Feats[/b][/h2]
[b]An important feedback we received from players[/b] was that most of our feats were just too passive - a flat bonus here and there, but nothing that would really change how you would play a character. [b]So we went back to the drawing board to bring a new set of feats [/b](as well as adjusting some existing ones)!
[list]	[*][b]Ambidextrous[/b]: +1 DEX, allows for dual-wielding with non-light 1 handed weapons[/*]	[*][b]Discretion of Coedymwarth[/b]: +1 DEX, grants proficiency with Light Armor, Shortsword, Shortbow and Longbow[/*]	[*][b]Eager for Battle[/b]: +1 DEX, grants advantage on initiative rolls[/*]	[*][b]Follow Up Strike[/b]: When attacking with a two-handed weapon, you can use a bonus action to deal an additional 1d4 + STR bonus damage of the same type[/*]	[*][b]Hauler[/b]: +1 STR, now doubles your carrying capacity (rather than increasing it by a flat 40 lbs)[/*]	[*][b]Might of the Iron Legion[/b]: Now requires proficiency with Medium Armor[/*]	[*][b]Powerful Cantrip[/b]: Now works with every cantrip that deals damage, not only ones with saving throws[/*]	[*][b]Raise Shield[/b]: When you are about to get hit by a ranged attack while wielding a shield, you can use your reaction to gain +3 AC until the end of the attacker's turn[/*]	[*][b]Rush to Battle[/b]: You can use your bonus action to increase your movement speed by 15', but you suffer -2 AC until the start of your next turn[/*]	[*][b]Sturdiness of the Tundra[/b]: +1 CON, grants proficiency with Medium Armor, Warhammer, Light Crossbow and Heavy Crossbow[/*]	[*][b]Take Aim[/b]: You can use your bonus action to negate all advantages and disadvantages on your ranged weapon attacks until the end of your turn[/*]	[*][b]Twin [/b][b]Blade[/b]: When you are about to get hit by a melee attack while dual-wielding (2 weapons), you can use your reaction to gain +3 AC until the end of the attacker's turn[/*]	[*][b]Uncanny Accuracy: [/b]Now works with all ranged attacks (including spells)[/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/7da487d49cc3164b4f2618be1f893f2f97df038b.png[/img]
[i]Longsword in one hand, Rapier in the other. With Ambidextrous, those d6 are turning into d8![/i]

[b]Our goal here was twofold - to give martial classes more options to use their bonus action and reaction, and to differentiate weapons playstyle[/b]. [b]Dual wielders[/b] now have access to [i]Ambidextrous [/i]and [i]Twin Blade[/i] to increase both their offensive and defensive options, [b]Two-handers[/b] can now dish out even more punishment with [i]Follow-Up Strike[/i], [b]Shield users[/b] can now use their shield to greater effect against ranged attacks with [i]Raise Shield[/i], and every [b]melee combattant[/b] benefits from [i]Rush to Battle[/i] to catch up to pesky ranged opponents. [b]Ranged characters[/b] can now also have a decent shot no matter the circumstances with [i]Take Aim[/i], and even [b]spellcasters [/b]are receiving some love with buffs to [i]Powerful Cantrip[/i] and [i]Uncanny Accuracy[/i].

While not everything might be perfectly balanced in these new options, we hope you'll give us plenty of feedback to finetune them - and [b]most of all, we hope you'll have fun with them[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/ff56f0de847f057cfb85b880a4833349ea74d567.png[/img]
[i]With Follow-Up Strike you get to smash things more often, which in my book is always a win.[/i]

[h2][b]Level Cap Increased to 8[/b][/h2]
[b]The Spring Update will also increase the level cap from 6 to 8, which will unlock the following:[/b]
[list]	[*][b]Every Class[/b]: An additional feat or ASI (Ability Score Improvement) at level 8[/*]	[*][b]Clerics[/b]: Level 4 spells & Level 8 Divine Domaine Feature (Note: Destroy Undead hasn't been implemented yet)[/*]	[*][b]Fighters[/b]: Level 7 Martial Archetype Feature[/*]	[*][b]Paladins[/b]: Level 7 Sacred Oath Feature[/*]	[*][b]Rangers[/b]: Level 7 Ranger Archetype Feature[/*]	[*][b]Rogue[/b]: Evasion[/*]	[*][b]Wizards[/b]: Level 4 Spells [/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/8a4a71118b89368151f804ddc60b64c18277c481.gif[/img]
[i]Here's a little level 5 Wall of Flame to warm up the room! (warning: friendly fire may occur)[/i]

[h2][b]Hunting Down the Early Game Difficulty Curves[/b][/h2]
Throughout the Winter Update we've seen a lot of players struggle against Soraks - and while [b]our reptilian foes are [/b][b]supposed to be challenging, we don't want them to become frustratin[/b][b]g either. [/b][b]There are two particular difficulty spikes early on [/b]that we identified: one being[b] the first time you face a Sorak party when trying to escape Caer Lem[/b] (in front of the firecamp), and two being [b]when you fight a large group of them after the library in the Tower of Magic[/b]. 
[list]	[*][b]In the first case[/b], it mostly comes from the fact that [b]the party had no access to long rest since the moment they arrived to Caer Lem[/b]. While more experience tabletop players know to conserve their resources, it's not exactly obvious for most players... Meaning quite a few parties had to face those Soraks with most if not all of their spell slots and class features expended already. This made for a tough fight, especially since it's due to choices made much earlier - so reloading at the start of the fight wouldn't really solve the difficulty spike. [/*]	[*][b]In the second case[/b], it's more due to [b]how action economy works at low level. [/b]At this stage of the game players have very little access to spells or features that can deal with multiple foes at once, so it's a simple case of being overrun by too many monsters - even if the monsters were weak (which is not the case here).[/*][/list]
[b]To make things a little more fair, [/b][b]we've removed one Sorak from both of these encounters[/b] to start with. Originally we expected the "surprise round" in these encounters to have a greater impact in leveling the playing field, but at the end of the day those fights were still a little too tough. [b]Note that if you find these fights too easy as a result, you can always pump up the challenge by tweaking the difficulty settings[/b] that will be added in the Spring Update. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/631c0bbda83d233509a1bd0e0ad339c8763ebfbc.png[/img]
[i]This encounter which previously featured 3 Warriors and 3 Saboteurs (6) is now 2 Warriors, 2 Saboteurs and 1 Skirmisher (5)[/i]

[b]There are many other encounters that we will tweak before launch, and not always to make them easier[/b] (for instance some of the later boss fights are a little too simple). However, [b]most won't be included in the Spring Update[/b] as we want to prioritize finishing the entire campaign before polishing the rough edges. We've also seen some more experienced tabletop players talking about encounter balance using CR. This is definitely something we're keeping an eye on, but [b]keep in mind that fights play out very differently on Tabletop and in a video game[/b]. This is why even though some encounters may be considered deadly when checking a CR encounter calculator, they seem very manageable in Solasta - monster AI, unlike human Dungeon Masters, don't adapt very well on the fly, and they can be far more predictable.

[h2][b]Revising the Soraks[/b][/h2]
Another issue in general with the Soraks is that[b] their stat bloc didn't mesh well with their intended CR level[/b]. This is partially because we originally designed the Soraks as if they were a playable race with class levels and such - which is a little bit of an older mindset dating back to the 3rd edition. Consequently, Soraks had similar traits to low level adventurers, with relatively low HP but high defensive capabilities (both AC and Saving Throws) - which were further boosted by the Child of Darkness buff when not under bright light conditions.

[b]That brought up two major issues:[/b]
[list]	[*]The first one is fairly obvious. [b]Higher AC and Saving Throws mean players would miss more often[/b], generating a lot of frustration for them. [/*]	[*]The second is more pernicious: Lower HP means that [b]if a fight went well, it felt very easy[/b] because Soraks would just die in a few hits - [b]creating a confirmation bias that nothing needed to be changed[/b] for those who rolled well during the encounter. [/*][/list]
So once again, [b]back to the drawing board we went[/b] - this time taking more time in comparing them with 5e monsters of similar CR. As a result, [b]we further fleshed out our different Sorak archetypes to give them more specific roles[/b]. Note that [b]these won't necessarily make them easier to face[/b] - some may even end up deadlier than before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/7f6982479fc2d59e09563b3c80f65934c9381db3.png[/img]
[i]You won't be confusing them with each other anymore! Read below for more explanation on what changed[/i]

[b]Sorak Skirmisher: [/b]The Skirmisher was a little too dangerous for its CR (1/2), especially since it was difficult to catch with its Shadow Escape power and the fact that it hid behind its beefier friends. As a consequence, we slightly lowered its AC, Dexterity Saving Throw, Attack Bonus and Damage Bonus, and its poison now deals 1d4 instead of 1d6. [b]Its role remains to stay far and chip away the party's HP.[/b]

[b]Sorak Warrior: [/b]Up until now, the Warrior felt like a bigger Skirmisher with very similar stats and slightly higher HP. To differentiate it from its ranged counterpart, the Sorak Warrior is now a big beefcake, with significantly more HP but less AC and a significantly weaker ranged attack (no poison). [b]Its role is reinforced into blocking the party from reaching more juicy targets behind it, but itself will be a little less dangerous than before. [/b]

[b]Sorak Saboteur:[/b] [b]The Saboteur remains in its role of mobile melee damage dealer[/b], with a nerf to their Dexterity Save which used to go through the roof and a little less poison damage (d4 instead d6) on their bite attack. It already had a fairly defined role compared to the two previous archetypes, as it trades its ranged attack with mobility, Doom Laughter and Call of the Night.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/3ef4bb3dbe0b5c36ba85dbef850ebd579c4b4c53.png[/img]
[i]Child of Darkness buff now scales, making it less of a headache to deal with at lower levels[/i]

Most importantly [b]we've made adjustments to the Child of Darkness buff, which[/b][b] now scales with the type of Sorak. [/b]Low CR Soraks like the Skirmisher, Warrior and Saboteur will receive a smaller buff overall (+1 instead of +2), and only when in Darkness (not in Dim Light) - while higher CR Soraks like the Acolyte will get a small buff in Dim Light, but a larger one in Darkness. Get your torches out folks! 

All in all these changes should make fights against Soraks not necessarily much easier, but at least [b]a little less RNG dependent[/b]. We invite you to give feedback once the Spring Update comes out to help us further fine tune them!

[h2][b]And what else? What else![/b][/h2]
Ohhh plenty more, but you'll have to come back next week to know! Can't have everything be spoiled straight away :D

[b]Alright folks, this is the end for today! [/b][b]Thank you for reading, and don't hesitate to drop by [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/]our Forums[/url] or [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]our Discord Server[/url].[/b]

notes.title: Dungeon Maker Showcase - Create your own Dungeons!
notes.content:
[i]Hey there folks,

You wanted it, we wanted it - modding tools to create your very own adventures in Solasta. We didn't make any promises back during our Kickstarter as we weren't sure we'd be able to make it before launch... But today we're happy to announce the Dungeon Maker - a map editor that will be accessible in-game to each and everyone of you! And we're not just making promises with a few screenshots here - here's a full video to show you what the Dungeon Maker is, and how it works![/i]

[previewyoutube=WkArBjQNIDM;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Will the Dungeon Maker be fully complete when Solasta 1.0 launches?[/b]	
[i]No, the Dungeon Maker will be in a beta state for quite some time - even after the 1.0 launch of Solasta. In order to have a playable version of the Dungeon Maker and avoid putting the main game at risk, we've decided to start small and add features as we go (rather than being too ambitious from the start).[/i]

[b]What are the current features of the Dungeon Maker?[/b]
[list]	[*][i]Freely create dungeon layouts using a selection of preset rooms[/i][/*]	[*][i]Link multiple maps together to create larger dungeons[/i][/*]	[*][i]One environment available for now, the Necropolis, with its set of environmental props to decorate your dungeon[/i][/*]	[*][i]Almost all monsters and items from Solasta: Crown of the Magister main campaign to create your encounters and loot[/i][/*]	[*][i]A selection of traps (just a few for now) to punish greedy adventurers[/i][/*]	[*][i]Easy to share online, it's a simple .json file in a folder. We plan to add Steam Workshop later on so it becomes even easier to share.[/i][/*][/list]
[b]What are the future features planned for the Dungeon Maker?[/b]	
[i]Provided we see people using the Dungeon Maker, we plan to add a Quest system, Merchants and other environments. After that... time will tell![/i]

[b]Can I import my own monsters / items in the Dungeon Maker?[/b]	
[i]No, at least not using the official Dungeon Maker tool on its own. That being said, it might become possible through the use of other community-created mods, as some have already started to create new classes and archetypes - so new items / monsters may not be an impossibility in the long run![/i]

[b]Where can I share my creation / download other people's Dungeon Maker maps?[/b]	
[i] While Solasta will eventually be on Steam Workshop later, in the meantime you could always take a look at [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/solastacrownofthemagister/][i][b]Nexusmod[/b] - where you can already find mods from community members[/i][/url][i] adding new feats, archetypes and other creative ideas! Note that we (Tactical Adventures) do not guarantee anything when it comes to user created mods - some may not work at all.[/i][/i]

[b]When will the Dungeon Maker be available?[/b]	
[i]Soon! That's all we can tell you for now :D[/i]

[h2][b]A little glimpse at the Adventure Book[/b][/h2]
Many of you Kickstarter Backers have been asking about the progress of our physical goods. We're happy to announce that [b]we've finished working on the digital version of the Adventure Book[/b] - a short adventure included in the Adventure Box - and will be moving onto completing the Adventure Box next, before starting the layout of the main Solasta Setting Sourcebook (which currently sports a meaty 180 pages!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/0dfc80d547c43ffb7996be9d5c5229544c5d4425.png[/img]
[i]This short adventure will take your party from level 1 to level 4 by diving deep into the Ruins of Carillach Gar![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/b8e867ccfd44677aedd704c7f9fb0d6d901515ce.png[/img]
[i]The Adventure Book should contain everything to help new DMs run their adventure without additional material[/i]

[b]Alright folks, this is the end for today! [/b][b]Thank you for reading, and don't hesitate to drop by [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/]our Forums[/url] or [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]our Discord Server[/url].[/b]

notes.title: Cracking Open The Difficulty Settings
notes.content:
[i]Hey there folks![/i]

[i]This week we'll be rolling Intelligence (Investigation) checks on the Difficulty Settings of Solasta. We briefly talked about them in a previous update, but it's time to get into the nitty gritty details - this way you'll know exactly your options at launch![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/684d47f5035667bc04c80cb1751ffb3554e3d56f.jpg[/img]
[i]But before that, let's give a warm hello to our 3D Programmer's sleepy doggo, Newt.[/i]

[h2][b]Preset Difficulty Settings[/b][/h2]
As with most games nowadays, [b]we will be offering you a few preset difficulty settings[/b] to choose from when you start a new adventure. Note that each of those preset [b]can be manually adjusted at any time [/b]during your campaign (we'll be going into more details in the next section). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/cd886025382e9660eae77c9263bb71fa31c62a46.png[/img]
[i]Iron Man has not yet been implemented, but we haven't forgotten about it![/i]

[b]Story Mode[/b], as its name implies, allows players who are not familiar with RPGs to simply enjoy the story. In this mode, damage taken by your party will be [b][i]severely reduced[/i][/b] and you will receive bonuses on most of your dice rolls, as well as having your [b][i]character automatically revive[/i][/b] at the end of each fight. [b][i]Some features are disabled[/i][/b], among which needing food to rest, having to roll concentration checks when hit and spellcasting being restrained by the spell components.

[b]Explorer Mode[/b] offers a more difficult challenge already. While the party still retains [b][i]some bonuses[/i][/b] to their rolls and a slight damage reduction, monsters will mostly be operating at [b][i]full capacity[/i][/b] so don't lure yourself into thinking that it will be a walk in the park. For players who aren't so familiar with the tabletop ruleset, Explorer Mode might be a good starting place. 

[b]Authentic Mode[/b] is the game as we, the Tactical Adventures crew, play it. [b][i]No modifiers[/i][/b], true RNG dice rolls that will make you curse the gods for making you miss 5 times in a row - only you, your characters, and the computer as a cold merciless DM. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/cf437476351b4a4f3e767d87da873e9c1094da21.png[/img]
[i]If you feel like the game is going too easy on you, Scavenger is here to spice things up![/i]

[b]Scavenger Mod[/b][b]e[/b] will go beyond, making monsters slighter tougher... [b][i]but much more vicious[/i][/b]! At that level of difficulty, monsters will start attacking unconscious characters to finish them off, try to shove characters off cliffs and use powerful moves more frequently (still within the ruleset limits though).

[b]Cataclysm Mode[/b] is there for those who've played the game in and out and are looking for the ultimate challenge. Monsters at this stage are not only vicious, they are also [b][i]incredibly beefed up[/i][/b] - on top of which [b][i]your party will receive 50% more damage[/i][/b] from any source. Prepare to die... A LOT.

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Battle[/b][/h2]
As mentioned above, you will be able to pick and choose difficulty settings to your liking - and you'll be able to do so whenever you want, even in the middle of a fight if you feel like things are getting too tough or too easy!
[list]	[*][b]Damage Taken: [/b]Sets the damage taken by your characters from 20% to 200% [i](default: 100%)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Disable Enemy Critical Hits: [/b]If activated, disables critical hits for your enemies [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Enemy Health Multiplier: [/b]Adjusts the max HP of your opponent from 50% to 300% of their original value [i](default: 100%)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/204325b6e213eadbea192eba6f56d98bd8a36538.png[/img]
[i]Health Multiplier in action! Slap some extra HP on them mobs if they die too quickly for your taste.[/i]
[list]	[*][b]Ally Saving Throw:[/b] Adds a modifier to your characters' Saving Throws from -10 to +10 [i](default: 0)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Enemy Saving Throw:[/b] Adds a modifier to your enemies' Saving Throws from -10 to +10 [i](default: 0)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Ally Attack Roll: [/b]Adds a modifier to your characters' Attack Rolls from -10 to +10 [i](default: 0)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Enemy Attack Roll: [/b]Adds a modifier to your enemies' Attack Rolls from -10 to +10 [i](default: 0)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/6816caad29936c9b9c09547ea30b111b54b41ee5.png[/img]
[i]+10 bonus to attack rolls? Parry this you filthy casual.[/i]
[list]	[*][b]Ally Ability Check:[/b] Adds a modifier to your characters Ability Checks, such as skill checks, from -10 to +10 [i](default: 0)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Enemy Ability Check: [/b]Adds a modifier to your enemies' Ability Checks, such as skill checks, from -10 to +10 [i](default: 0)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Deadlier AI: [/b]If activated, monsters will use their powerful moves (such as large AoE spells or powers) [b][i]more frequently, although still within the ruleset limits[/i][/b] - as well as attempt to shove characters into bottomless pits if given the chance. Off by default to avoid the frustration of being showered with lightning bolts straight off the bat when facing spellcasters, or having monsters open with their most powerful move too often [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Merciless AI: [/b]If activated, monsters will now target unconscious characters on purpose to finish them off [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Autorevive:[/b] If activated, characters will automatically revive at the end of a fight as long as one party member is still standing [i](default: off)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/fefc0bf8048d2826d03cd1da47fa374263550356.gif[/img]
[i]Are they gone now? No no no I wasn't dead, I was merely pretending.[/i]

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Health & Rest Settings[/b][/h2]
[list]	[*][b]Companions Rest: [/b]Critical NPCs and companions fully recover their HP when doing a short rest [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]No Food Required: [/b]Long rest no longer require rations [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Max Health on Hit Dice:[/b] When recovering HP during a short rest, Hit Dice will always roll their maximum value [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Max Health on Level Up:[/b] Sets the maximum HP of all party members to the maximum value allowed by their Hit Dice. [b][i]This option is retroactive[/i][/b], meaning if you activate it your level 6 Fighter with 18 CON would see their max HP become (10 + 4) x 6 = 84. [b][i]Deactivating it will also reset the party members max HP to their original value[/i][/b] - in this example, our level 6 Fighter with 18 CON would go back to (10 + 4) + (6 + 4) x 5 = 64 max HP [i](default: off)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/4aa4b968ae4909431d67d6102807fba3f97a84aa.png[/img]
[i]What do you mean, "am I cheating"? I absolutely rolled 10 on every single level up, promise![/i]

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Inventory[/b][/h2]
There are three different options for the [b]Encumbrance Rule[/b] [i](default: Solasta)[/i]
[list]	[*][b]Tabletop: [/b]Characters can carry up to [b][i]15x[/i][/b] their STR score, as per the official tabletop ruleset [/*]	[*][b]Solasta (Variant): [/b]Characters can carry up to [b][i]15x [/i][/b]their STR score, but will be [b][i]encumbered above 5x[/i][/b] and [b][i]heavily encumbered above 10x[/i][/b][/*]	[*][b]Simplified: [/b]Characters can carry up to [b][i]150x[/i][/b] their STR score - making their bags effectively portable black holes[/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/47796e68280c588657e5457b853466eb707030f7.png[/img]
[i]Loot goblins rejoice, you can pick up everything and render Scavengers obsolete! They are now unemployed! Are you happy, you heartless monsters?[/i]

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Spellcasting & Spell Components[/b][/h2]
[list]	[*][b]Never Lose Concentration:[/b] If activated, your spellcasters will no longer roll concentration checks when taking damage [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Universal Scrolls:[/b] If activated, scrolls will be usable by anyone. By default, scrolls can only be used by a character if the spell exists in their class' spell list [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Verbal Components:[/b] If activated, spells with the Verbal component can no longer be cast if the caster is Silenced [i](default: on)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Somatic Components:[/b] If activated, spells with the Somatic component will require a free hand to be cast. Two-handed weapons like quarterstaves don't prevent the casting of Somatic spells [i](default: on)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Material Components: [/b]If [b][i]Basic mode[/i][/b] is activated, spells with the Material component will require a spell focus or component pouch to be equipped to be cast. If [b][i]Full mode[/i][/b] is activated, some spells will also require specific items to be available in your inventory - such as a pearl for Identify or a diamond for Revivify [i](default: basic) [/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/75ec1a1150d4613f5c4b2573e73d49be64bd0cf9.png[/img]
[i]Why yes, casting magic is complicated my good man! Without the proper conditions I cannot make miracles happen[/i]

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Dice Rolls[/b][/h2]
There are two options for the [b]Random Mode[/b][i] (default: True Random)[/i]
[list]	[*][b]True Random:[/b] Better pray to the gods of RNG, because true random can absolutely shaft you with multiple bad rolls in a row. Just like real dice. That's why dice prison is a thing.[/*]	[*][b]Karmic Dice:[/b] For those who are tired of being on the receiving end of the fickle RNG gods, the [b][i]Karmic Dice options will accumulate luck[/i][/b] whenever you roll poorly or when your opponents roll particularly well. [b][i]High luck will greatly affect your chances of getting good rolls[/i][/b] as well as your opponents' chances of getting bad rolls, and will slowly decrease when you get good rolls. Note that there is no negative luck - Karmic Dice can only help you. [b][i]At 0 luck, the dice behavior is the same as True Random[/i][/b][/*][/list]
Other than that, there are two other options that impact the Dice Roll:
[list]	[*][b]Guaranteed Critical:[/b] If activated, the game will guarantee to roll a 20 for the player at least once every 15 rolls [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Preserve Random Seed:[/b] Although not a difficulty setting, many players are used to reloading saves hoping to get better rolls when playing Tactical RPGs. This option, which is activated by default, prevents save scumming by preserving the random seed - meaning if you roll a 1, then reload to try again, you will just roll another 1. [b][i]Deactivating this option allows you to roll a new number after reloading[/i][/b]. Preserve Random Seed can be found in the Gameplay section, at the top of the Game Settings tab [i](default: on)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/24da7b605ea20123a37bf417ebca6215ea888564.png[/img]
[i]Deactivate that option and save-scum away! No one's judging you, it's a single player game[/i]

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Story[/b][/h2]
[list]	[*][b]Force Dialog Roll Success:[/b] If activated, you will automatically succeed any skill checks during dialogs. Makes Intimidation, Persuasion, Deception and Insight obsolete[i] (default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Always Display Dialog Chances:[/b] If activated, you will automatically see the success chances of any skill check during dialogs. Makes Insight obsolete [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Unlock All Bestiary: [/b]If activated, unlocks all bestiary entries.[b][i] If deactivated during the campaign, the bestiary will still retain the information of the monsters you already faced[/i][/b], provided you succeeded on your skill check to gather information [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Disable Random Encounter: [/b]If activated, disables random encounters when traveling on the World Map[i] (default: off)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/c26d390ee3c405598f73cf0260e8145110fa733e.png[/img]
[i]Honestly though, slowly filling your Poked... - I mean bestiary - on your own is a pretty fun thing to do![/i]

[h2][b]Custom Difficulty - Exploration[/b][/h2]
[list]	[*][b]Reroll Exploration Checks: [/b]If activated, allows you to reroll skill checks during exploration as many times as you want. By default, failing to open a open a lock or disarm a trap will prevent you from trying again [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Autodetect Traps:[/b] If activated, traps will be automatically detected when you get close to them [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]No Tool Required: [/b]If activated, characters will be able to craft and unlock doors without needing to have the proper tools in their inventory [i](default: off)[/i][/*]	[*][b]Force Crafting Roll Success:[/b] If activated, crafting rolls will always be successful [i](default: off)[/i][/*][/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/2824bd5634c940a6218cda739e07c78ff488ada9.png[/img]
[i]That's for all of you folks out there who can't find the damn Manacalon Rosary. Where the hell is it?![/i]

[b]Alright folks, this is the end for today! [/b][b]Thank you for reading, and don't hesitate to drop by [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/]our Forums[/url] or [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]our Discord Server[/url].[/b]

Digging?[/url][/*]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/115-kickstarter-rewards-february-update]Kickstarter Rewards - February Update[/url][/*]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/114-dev-update-27-whats-cooking-beyond-wizards-tower]Dev Update #27 - What's cooking beyond Wizard's Tower?[/url][/*][/list]

Enemy Saving Throw: Adds a modifier to your enemies' Saving Throws from -10 to +10 (default: 0)
Ally Attack Roll: Adds a modifier to your characters' Attack Rolls from -10 to +10 (default: 0)
Enemy Attack Roll: Adds a modifier to your enemies' Attack Rolls from -10 to +10 (default: 0)
Ally Ability Check: Adds a modifier to your characters Ability Checks, such as skill checks, from -10 to +10 (default: 0)
Enemy Ability Check: Adds a modifier to your enemies' Ability Checks, such as skill checks, from -10 to +10 (default: 0)

Deadlier AI: If activated, monsters will use their powerful moves (such as large AoE spells or powers) more frequently, although still within the ruleset limits - as well as attempt to shove characters into bottomless pits if given the chance. Off by default to avoid the frustration of being showered with lightning bolts straight off the bat when facing spellcasters, or having monsters open with their most powerful move too often (default: off)
Merciless AI: If activated, monsters will now target unconscious characters on purpose to finish them off (default: off)
Autorevive: If activated, characters will automatically revive at the end of a fight as long as one party member is still standing (default: off)
Companions Rest: Critical NPCs and companions fully recover their HP when doing a short rest (default: off)
No Food Required: Long rest no longer require rations (default: off)
Max Health on Hit Dice: When recovering HP during a short rest, Hit Dice will always roll their maximum value (default: off)

Max Health on Level Up: Sets the maximum HP of all party members to the maximum value allowed by their Hit Dice. This option is retroactive, meaning if you activate it your level 6 Fighter with 18 CON would see their max HP become (10 + 4) x 6 = 84. Deactivating it will also reset the party members max HP to their original value - in this example, our level 6 Fighter with 18 CON would go back to (10 + 4) + (6 + 4) x 5 = 64 max HP (default: off)
There are three different options for the Encumbrance Rule (default: Solasta)
Tabletop: Characters can carry up to 15x their STR score, as per the official tabletop ruleset
Solasta (Variant): Characters can carry up to 15x their STR score, but will be encumbered above 5x and heavily encumbered above 10x
Simplified: Characters can carry up to 150x their STR score - making their bags effectively portable black holes
Never Lose Concentration: If activated, your spellcasters will no longer roll concentration checks when taking damage (default: off)
Universal Scrolls: If activated, scrolls will be usable by anyone. By default, scrolls can only be used by a character if the spell exists in their class' spell list (default: off)
Verbal Components: If activated, spells with the Verbal component can no longer be cast if the caster is Silenced (default: on)

Somatic Components: If activated, spells with the Somatic component will require a free hand to be cast. Two-handed weapons like quarterstaves don't prevent the casting of Somatic spells (default: on)

Material Components: If Basic mode is activated, spells with the Material component will require a spell focus or component pouch to be equipped to be cast. If Full mode is activated, some spells will also require specific items to be available in your inventory - such as a pearl for Identify or a diamond for Revivify (default: basic)
There are two options for the Random Mode (default: True Random)
True Random: Better pray to the gods of RNG, because true random can absolutely shaft you with multiple bad rolls in a row. Just like real dice. That's why dice prison is a thing.

Karmic Dice: For those who are tired of being on the receiving end of the fickle RNG gods, the Karmic Dice options will accumulate luck whenever you roll poorly or when your opponents roll particularly well. High luck will greatly affect your chances of getting good rolls as well as your opponents' chances of getting bad rolls, and will slowly decrease when you get good rolls. Note that there is no negative luck - Karmic Dice can only help you. At 0 luck, the dice behavior is the same as True Random
Guaranteed Critical: If activated, the game will guarantee to roll a 20 for the player at least once every 15 rolls (default: off)

Preserve Random Seed: Although not a difficulty setting, many players are used to reloading saves hoping to get better rolls when playing Tactical RPGs. This option, which is activated by default, prevents save scumming by preserving the random seed - meaning if you roll a 1, then reload to try again, you will just roll another 1. Deactivating this option allows you to roll a new number after reloading. Preserve Random Seed can be found in the Gameplay section, at the top of the Game Settings tab (default: on)
Force Dialog Roll Success: If activated, you will automatically succeed any skill checks during dialogs. Makes Intimidation, Persuasion, Deception and Insight obsolete (default: off)
Always Display Dialog Chances: If activated, you will automatically see the success chances of any skill check during dialogs. Makes Insight obsolete (default: off)

Unlock All Bestiary: If activated, unlocks all bestiary entries. If deactivated during the campaign, the bestiary will still retain the information of the monsters you already faced, provided you succeeded on your skill check to gather information (default: off)
Disable Random Encounter: If activated, disables random encounters when traveling on the World Map (default: off)

Reroll Exploration Checks: If activated, allows you to reroll skill checks during exploration as many times as you want. By default, failing to open a open a lock or disarm a trap will prevent you from trying again (default: off)
Autodetect Traps: If activated, traps will be automatically detected when you get close to them (default: off)
No Tool Required: If activated, characters will be able to craft and unlock doors without needing to have the proper tools in their inventory (default: off)
Force Crafting Roll Success: If activated, crafting rolls will always be successful (default: off)

notes.title: Dev Diary #28 - Side Quests, Monsters and... Digging?
notes.content:
[i]Hey there folks![/i]

[i]Following a bit of misunderstanding from our article 2 weeks ago, we've decided to rename our Dev Updates to Dev Diaries - so that people don't end up thinking they were linked with actual game patches. For those who've only started following us recently, we've been calling this line of articles Dev Updates from the very start - as they were updates on what the Tactical Adventures crew was working on. However since "Update" could also be viewed as a "Game Update" (or patch) now that the game is actually available on Steam, it was understandably making some people confused. Anyway enough prattling, let's move on to the meat and potatoes of this week![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/a69bc9c42b6a0a53fa3e0ee1b22cac6508aafe32.png[/img]
[i]That's it, you can stop reading now. We all know what you're really here for.[/i]

[h2][b]Side quests, reporting for duty![/b][/h2]
Now that we've have a sizeable chunk of the main campaign playable, [b]we've started working on adding some side quests into the mix[/b]! This should hopefully alleviate the feeling of the game being too linear, forcing you to rush down the main quest from one mission to another. [b]That being said remember that Solasta is not intended to be an open world game[/b] -  side quests are meant to enhance the overall experience, which is still focused on the main campaign. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/c96cf2c8a45b74640780cd2dd998a7140101bc07.png[/img]
[i]Here's a little glimpse into one of the 8 Background Quests, which availability will depend on your characters' background[/i]

[b]We plan to have two major types of side quests in Solasta[/b]. The first type, shown in the screenshot above, are fairly elaborate quests with cutscenes and oftentimes handcrafted levels - for instance, Background Quests and the Legendary Quest mentioned [url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/115-kickstarter-rewards-february-update]in last week's article[/url]. The second type are more straightforward quests with little in the way of narration, such as pickup quests asking you to clear a pack of monsters in an old location you've already visited for example. Those are mostly here to give you a little break from the story and encourage you to visit (or revisit) locations to make sure you're not missing out some cool loot and experience. That said, do not worry - you can absolutely ignore all of that and focus on the main quest if you prefer. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/f1778d9f514ea081166b0cf9a854d7a95d5ed345.png[/img]
[i]Another peek, this time looking at another Background Quest under construction. Let's see if you can recognize it once it is implemented in-game![/i]

[h2][b]Digging a hole[/b][/h2]
No, I don't mean you - put the shovel away. Let me tell you a little story, one about the early days of Solasta. [b]Originally, when we talked about the 3D aspect of Solasta, we dreamt big[/b] - we wanted creatures flying in the sky, swimming in the water, breaking through walls and burrowing underground. Now as always, when you have to sit down and actually make the game, [b]you need to scope and prioritize so that you don't end up running out of time and money with a half-finished mess on your hands[/b].

This is why of everything I mentioned above, flying is the only thing that made it into the game so far - although trust me, we really, really wanted that minotaur to be able to charge through and pulverize thin walls, but we just couldn't fit that in. [b]And it is also why we've had creatures that can burrow in our design bucket for such a long time![/b]

Now, before you go and get hyped about creatures actually being able to move under the map (as if they were flying, but inside the ground), let me cut that short. We thought about it, and it was creating a whole lot of problems - problems which we wouldn't have time to solve, such as creating an entirely new pathfinding AI just for these creatures so that they don't end up getting stuck between two rocks because the level isn't completely flat. [b]Instead, burrowing will work like this.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/eb5b88d02b7bc4f223aefe40bcd676866355f696.gif[/img]
[i]No, giant burrowing Minotaurs won't happen. This is just us testing the feature.[/i]

[b]Now you just have to imagine the monster not being a minotaur, having a burrowing animation and some FX of soil flying around as it burrows in / out of the ground[/b]. What do you mean, "that's everything"? You want me to curse your dice rolls with bad RNG, is that it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/28484505dae32cba55ced25376e92178aed43f48.png[/img]
[i]Here come the Redeemers, the bane of all spellcasters![/i]

[h2][b]I want to see it move[/b][/h2]
Now when we show you new monsters in Dev Diaries, it's sometimes hard to picture how they will really look like once they are implemented in-game.[b] Which is why our lead animator has made a few gifs for us to share with you![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/722fbf986ea88d926570e71add707cfbe4c21cf1.gif[/img]
[i]Swiggity swooty I'm comin' for that booty[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/529b4274ca523d6ff3332b3107dc17624d2cca32.gif[/img]
[i]Did I mention it can swallow you whole if it grapples you?[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/820b5cb31db1725f03c705a9bcde1614804837a7.gif[/img]
[i]A little work in progress animation of our big fat Ogre playing around with his javelin.[/i]

[h2][b]A little side of art to go with with that?[/b][/h2]
As our Art Team has been very productive, it would be a shame to leave you without a little bit of everything they did during the last few weeks. [b]Feast your eyes upon these babies![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/0a04536fd0196f98d08b5e3a7d380ac1b9cbca43.jpg[/img]
[i]Wait, I thought you were joking when you said "the floor is lava".[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/25f769450bdb6dcd70345f866bedd5c27d2720d9.png[/img]
[i]Do you recognize this place? [/i][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/storage/314/conversions/abyss_hd1920-pinned.jpg][i]It's the Concept Art of the level[/i][/url][i]![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/2696d05dc599e20c73d5ad2bc0252dd50ce71a5b.png[/img]
[i]I'm always impressed by the level of details that goes into the props made by our 3D Environment Artist[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/bd33013197c61c56f2be834d788e899346bfea97.gif[/img]
[i]Banishment, 4th level Abjuration spell[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/e971bee54d4e37d8a2615661deb69f718535f8c3.gif[/img]
[i]Death Ward, 4th level Abjuration spell[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/00ff0097463c8ed6b72800d84d013369aa0c5e28.gif[/img]
[i]Dimension Door, 4th level Conjuration spell[/i]

[b]Alright folks, this is the end for today! [/b][b]Thank you for reading, and don't hesitate to drop by [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/]our Forums[/url] or [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]our Discord Server[/url].[/b]

notes.title: Dev Update #27 - What's cooking beyond Wizard's Tower?
notes.content:
[i]Hey there folks![/i]

[i]With all the recent patch notes and other articles about community feedback and bug fixing, we haven't been showing you a lot of new stuff lately. This is something we intend to fix... today, now, this very round! In fact, stop whatever you're doing and roll initiative, we're getting right down to business![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/aefd1ab2d19f2bad6fba370c3478801d65813c3e.jpg[/img]
[i]... But first, here's our weekly cat allowance.[/i]

[h2][b]Fire in the Hole![/b][/h2]
You know it, we know it, the adventure does not end at the Wizard's Tower. [b]Your party will be going ever deeper into the Badlands, entering orc territory next[/b]. Now, there are tons of things we'd love to share with you - but we also do not wish to spoil everything, which is why you'll have to make do with a few pictures for now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/70120fceb1fc15a28ab6889c8adcf01319552898.jpg[/img]
[i]Step forward brave adventurers, and enter our lair...[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/f1f1fb53b6f6c94b9068752f8aed20cf414e3a8f.jpg[/img]
[i]Hope you don't mind the heat! Oh and watch your footing, or pray you succeed your Dexterity saving throw.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/eb0dc4b302870518802f76b4050ce20a9895ae99.jpg[/img]
[i]Welcome home, such as it is. This squalid hamlet, these corrupted lands... wait wrong game I'm being told.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/088765634815fbed0c7bde7dd56b4bee37dc8d39.png[/img]
[i]"But what will it look like in-game?" I hear you asking. Well ask no more, that right there is a screenshot.[/i]

[h2][b]Preparing a New Batch of Monsters[/b][/h2]
Goblins and Ghosts, Ghosts 'n Goblins... I'm sure you want some new foes to face by now, right? This is why we've been hard at work on a new monster... [b]the female orc![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/846fcf229c8462edede878974a9ddefec70539e8.png[/img]
[i]What's better than orcs? More orcs![/i]

Alright alright lower your pitchforks, sheesh! Guess that's what I get for dumping Charisma, can't roll a good Performance check to save my life. Jokes aside, [b]we now have female orcs ready to go for when your party meets the orc tribes later during the campaign[/b]. And let me tell you, if you expect orcs to simply be savage monsters, you'll be in for a shock.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/b0cfdaafb15b5d06e0b2e787915a44c053bcb8e3.png[/img]
[i]Storm, Earth and Fire, heed my call![/i]

[b]Without any transition, give a warm welcome to our new elemental friends! [/b]Wait... what's that? Sorry, I'm being told they might not be as friendly as I first expected. Fighting might occur, deadly injuries might ensue - consider yourself warned. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/e51d4243b3da39d251c42d6b6b65ed2f70068f2d.png[/img]
[i]What's 40 feet long, CR 11 and devours adventurers for breakfast?[/i]

[b]If you answered "Remorhaz", you are correct! [/b]Everyone else go back to studying the Monster Manual, it will be on the next test so pay attention during class. [b]This mighty beast was introduced to Solasta by the community during our Kickstarter campaign[/b], and will take a lot of preparation to take down. Able to swallow its target whole with a simple bite, the Remorhaz has spelled the end of many would-be heroes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/2439750b446f68b959f44c7201e6f7da5ea48d30.png[/img]
[i]Giant beetles? Were giant spiders not enough?[/i]

For those who joined the Solastan community recently, you might be a little confused by the picture above. Giant beetles? What are those? [b]Well, say hello to your spellcasters' new nightmare: the Redeemers.[/b] These gigantic insects, originally created by the old elven empire, thrived in the Badlands in the absence of their former masters - [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/forum/community-vote-from-whence-cometh-the-redeemers][b]and they have evolved in some of the worst way possible.[/b][/url]

[h2][b]My Tailor is Rich![/b][/h2]
For our non-French friends, know that for some reason this was one of the first english sentence we would be taught back in the old days. And yes, it served as much as you would expect (hint: as much as a barbarian dip in a high level wizard build). Anyway, lore dump aside we have good news for you. [b]Our magic armours are now looking better than ever, which will distinguish them from their regular counterpart![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/e240153195cad0f91aba5c20dc5d81cdb03fe3db.png[/img]
[i]Now you can slay while looking dapper! No, that does not mean I'm giving you a bonus in Charisma for free though.[/i]

[h2][b]Putting That Code to Work[/b][/h2]
While our Art team produces most of what we usually show in our Dev Updates, it's good to remember that our programmers are still hard at work. [b]We've recently implemented quite a few improvements, such as preventing different characters from stacking onto one another while exploring or having characters orient themselves towards their enemy when taking a hit. [/b]That being said, one of the biggest improvements we're currently adding to the game are [b]difficulty options[/b]. We've been talking about it for quite some time, but we've just now implemented it in-game - see for yourself! We'll go into more details in a future article about everything you can switch on and off in those settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/60b6ce5ea4abdfd45b27c0aad20a64701e3c59df.gif[/img]
[i]What options do you want? All of them. You get to pick and choose what you want.[/i]

[h2][b]A Few Spells for the Road?[/b][/h2]
It's been quite some time since we shared some new spells, hasn't it? Those were good times. So good in fact that I've got some available to go around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/7c055f0949b3ae636b2a7b43fd8d377cce62f573.gif[/img]
[i]Grease, 1st level conjuration spell[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/b8a566591bf9771d9acd18532bf476aacd03d952.gif[/img]
[i]Silence, 2nd level illusion spell[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35306982/ff719747ace30a2ba0a7f1ccff133ecb7536d5e5.gif[/img]
Sleet Storm, 3rd level conjuration spell[/i]

[b]Alright folks, this is the end for today! [/b][b]Thank you for reading, and don't hesitate to drop by [url=https://forums.solasta-game.com/]our Forums[/url] or [url=https://discord.com/invite/uu8utaF]our Discord Server[/url].[/b]

[b]Read our previous articles here:[/b]
[list]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/113-solasta-january-patch-patch-notes]Solasta January Patch - Patch Notes[/url][/*]	[*][url=https://www.solasta-game.com/news/112-dev-update-26-welcome-2021-community-feedback-2]Dev Update #26 - Welcome 2021 & Community Feedback #2![/url][/*][/list]

[i]Article by Tactical Myzzrym[/i]
